name: Heightfield Rendering
definition: A software rendering technique that projects a 2D heightfield map onto a 2D screen by casting rays from the camera through the screen width at increasing depth intervals (LOD), calculating screen-space Y positions for terrain heights, and drawing vertical lines to fill the screen from the terrain surface to the horizon (hidden surface removal via a per-column height buffer).
summary: Heightfield Rendering projects 2D heightmaps onto screens via discrete view-Z planes and per-column occlusion buffers, optimizing performance with variable column widths and increasing depth intervals.
